source_text: τοὺς αἰῶνας, εἰ μὴ ὁ μονογενής; 32.20 τίνες δὲ οἱ ἀλλάξαντες τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ; 32.21 οἱ λέγοντες· «δόξα πατρὶ δι' υἱοῦ ἐν ἁγίῳ πνεύματι», οἱ καὶ κτίσμα αὐτὸν καὶ οὐδὲ βασιλέα αἰώνιον δοξάζοντες. 32.22 Εἶτα τοῖς αὐτοῖς φησιν· «εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτοὺς ἀναπολογήτους, διότι γνόντες θεὸν οὐχ ὡς θεὸν ἐδόξα σαν ἢ ηὐχαρίστησαν, ἀλλ' ἐματαιώθησαν ἐν τοῖς διαλογισμοῖς αὐτῶν, καὶ ἐσκοτίσθη ἡ ἀσύνετος αὐτῶν καρδία». 32.23 ποῖος δὲ ὁ γνωσθεὶς θεὸς καὶ μὴ ἐπιγνωσθεὶς παρὰ αἱρετικῶν καὶ Ἰουδαίων καὶ Ἑλλήνων, εἰ μὴ ὁ ἐπιφανεὶς σαρκὶ θεὸς λόγος; 32.24 Καὶ Κορινθίοις δὲ ἐν τοῖς πρώτοις γράμμασι κύριον δόξης κατὰ φύσιν εἶναι δεικνὺς αὐτὸν ἐπιστέλλει οὕτως· 32.25 «εἰ γὰρ ᾔδεσαν, οὐκ ἂν τὸν κύριον τῆς δόξης ἐσταύρωσαν», 32.26 καὶ ἑτέρωθι· «ἵνα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ πᾶν γόνυ κάμψῃ καὶ πᾶσα γλῶσσα ἐξο μολογήσεται, ὅτι κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς εἰς δόξαν θεοῦ πατρός», ἀντὶ τοῦ· ἐν αὐτῇ τῇ πατρικῇ δόξῃ ὑπάρχει. 32.27 Καὶ ἔτι· «τὸν γὰρ ἠλαττωμένον βλέπομεν Ἰησοῦν διὰ τὸ πάθημα τοῦ θανάτου δόξῃ καὶ τιμῇ ἐστεφανωμένον». 32.28 ὑστεροπρώτως εἴρηται. φησὶν γάρ· τὸν δοκοῦντά τισιν διὰ τὸ πάθημα τοῦ θανάτου ἠλαττῶσθαι Ἰησοῦν βλέπομεν δόξῃ καὶ τιμῇ ἐστεφανωμένον. 32.29 Ἀλλὰ καὶ δόξαν αὐτὸν καλεῖ ἅτε φυσικῶς ἀπαύγασμα ὄντα τῆς πατρικῆς δόξης, δι' ὧν γράφει· «ὁ θεὸς τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ πατὴρ τῆς δόξης». 32.30 θεὸν δὲ εἶπεν τῆς ἀρρήτου σαρκώσεως, πατέρα δὲ τῆς ἀνάρχου γεννήσεως. 32.31 Καὶ πάλιν Ἰωάννης· «ἐθεασάμεθα τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, δόξαν ὡς μονογενοῦς παρὰ πατρός, πλήρης χάριτος καὶ ἀληθείας». 32.32 καὶ πάλιν παρὰ Μάρκῳ μὲν ἀπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος· «ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς ἐν τῇ δόξῃ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ» παριστῶν, ὡς ἡ αὐτοῦ δόξα ἰσότιμος τῆς δόξης ἐστὶν τοῦ πατρός· 32.33 παρὰ δὲ Ματθαίῳ· «ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντες οἱ ἄγγελοι αὐτοῦ μετ' αὐτοῦ». 32.34 Καὶ αὖθις γοῦν Ἰωάννης συνιστῶν τὸ ἐν δόξῃ εἶναι αὐτὸν καὶ παρὰ πάντων δόξαν ὀφείλεσθαι αὐτῷ εἶπεν· «τοσαῦτα δὲ σημεῖα πεποιηκότος τοῦ Ἰησοῦ οὐκ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι, ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ Ἠσαΐου· ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε». 32.35 καὶ μεταξὺ ἐπάγει· «ταῦτα δὲ εἶπεν, ὅτε εἶδεν τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐλάλησεν περὶ αὐτοῦ». 32.36 Καὶ Πέτρος δὲ ἐν μὲν τῇ πρώτῃ ἐπιστολῇ· «καθ' ὃ κοινωνεῖτε τοῖς τοῦ Χριστοῦ παθήμασιν χαίρετε, ἵνα καὶ ἐν τῇ ἀποκαλύψει τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ χαρῆτε ἀγαλλιώμενοι»· 32.37 ἐν δὲ τῇ δευτέρᾳ· «ὡς τὰ πάντα ἡμῖν τῆς θείας δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ τὰ πρὸς ζωὴν καὶ εὐσέβειαν δεδωρημένης διὰ τῆς ἐπιγνώσεως τοῦ καλέσαντος ἡμᾶς ἰδίᾳ δόξῃ καὶ ἀρε τῇ» ἀντὶ τοῦ· «ἡ δόξα τοῦ μονογενοῦς ἡ τῆς φύσεως, ἡ τῶν θαυμάτων, ἡ τῆς βασιλείας καὶ αὐτῆς τῆς δοξολογίας ὁμοία ἐστιν καὶ ἴση τῆς δόξης τοῦ πατρός, παρ' οὗ φυσικῶς καὶ ἀδιαστάτως γεγέννηται, καὶ ὅλα ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἔχει ὡς μονογενής, ὥστε καὶ γενόμενον σάρκα μηδεμίαν τροπὴν ἢ μείωσιν ὑπομεῖναι». 32.38 Οὕτω καὶ οἱ τρεῖς παῖδες οὐ τῇ Βαβυλωνίᾳ φλογί, ἀλλὰ τῷ περὶ τὸν κτίστην καὶ εὐεργέτην πυρακτούμενοι πόθῳ καὶ οὐ μᾶλλον τὴν περιβάλλουσαν αὐτοὺς κάμινον τῆς ἡτοιμασμένης τοῖς κτιστολάτραις γεέννης προσέχοντες ὑπέβαλλον τῇ κτίσει δοξολογεῖν τὸν φανέντα σὺν αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ καμίνῳ περὶ οὗ γέγραπται «ἡ δὲ ὅρασις τοῦ τετάρτου ὁμοία υἱῷ θεοῦ»: 32.39 «εὐλογεῖτε, πάντα τὰ ἔργα κυρίου, τὸν κύριον· ὑμνεῖτε καὶ ὑπερυψοῦτε αὐτὸν εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας». 32.40 Ἀχθομένων δέ, φησίν, καὶ τῶν κυριοκτόνων πρὸς τὰ παιδία καὶ τοὺς ὄχλους ὅτι ὡς θεὸν τὸν Ἰησοῦν δοξάζοντες ἔλεγον· «ὠσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις· εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου», ὑπέμνησεν αὐτοὺς τῆς λεγούσης γραφῆς· «ἐκ στόματος νηπίων καὶ θηλαζόντων κατηρτίσω αἶνον» ἑαυτῷ ἁρμόσας τὸ ῥητὸν τοῦτο καὶ δείξας μὴ ἀνοικείως προσάγεσθαι αὐτῷ δόξαν. 32.41 καὶ ἄγγελοι δέ, φησίν,
pass_a_gloss: [...into] the ages, if not the only-begotten? 32.20 And who are the ones who exchanged his glory? 32.21 The ones saying: 'glory to the Father through the Son in the Holy Spirit', the ones glorifying him also as a creature and not even as an eternal king. 32.22 Then to the same ones he says: 'so that they be without defence, because having known God they did not glorify him as God or give thanks, but were made vain in their reasonings, and their unintelligent heart was darkened'. 32.23 And what sort is the God known and not recognized by heretics and Jews and Greeks, if not the God Word who appeared in flesh? 32.24 And to the Corinthians also in the first letter, showing him to be Lord of glory according to nature, he writes thus: 32.25 'for if they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of the glory', 32.26 and in another place: 'that in the name of Jesus Christ every knee should bend and every tongue will confess that Jesus Christ is Lord into the glory of God the Father', in place of [saying]: he subsists in the paternal glory itself. 32.27 And further: 'for the one having been made less we see, Jesus, on account of the suffering of death, with glory and honour crowned'. 32.28 It has been said in later-first order. For he says: Jesus, the one seeming to some to have been made less on account of the suffering of death, we see crowned with glory and honour. 32.29 But he also calls him glory, as being by nature a radiance of the paternal glory, through the words in which he writes: 'the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of the glory'. 32.30 He said God of the unspeakable enfleshment, and Father of the beginningless begetting. 32.31 And again John: 'we gazed on his glory, glory as of an only-begotten from a father, full of grace and truth'. 32.32 And again in Mark, from the Saviour: 'whenever the Son comes in the glory of his Father', presenting that his glory is of equal honour with the glory of the Father; 32.33 and in Matthew: 'whenever the Son of Man comes in his glory and all his angels with him'. 32.34 And once more indeed John, establishing his being in glory and that glory is owed to him from all, said: 'Jesus having done so many signs, the Jews did not believe into him, so that the thing spoken through Isaiah be fulfilled: with hearing you will hear and by no means understand'. 32.35 And in between he brings on: 'these things he said when he saw his glory, and spoke about him'. 32.36 And Peter also, in the first letter: 'in so far as you share in the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, so that also in the uncovering of his glory you may rejoice exulting'; 32.37 and in the second: 'as his divine power has gifted us all the things toward life and piety through the full knowledge of the one who called us by his own glory and excellence', in place of: the glory of the only-begotten, that of the nature, that of the wonders, that of the kingdom and of the glorification itself, is like and equal to the glory of the Father, from whom by nature and without gap he has been begotten, and he holds the wholes in himself as only-begotten, so that even having become flesh he endured no turning or lessening. 32.38 Thus also the three boys, glowing red-hot not with the Babylonian flame but with yearning toward the founder and benefactor, and heeding not more the furnace around them than the Gehenna made ready for the creature-worshippers, were suggesting to the creation to glorify the one who appeared with them in the furnace, about whom it has been written 'and the sight of the fourth is like to a son of God': 32.39 'bless the Lord, all the works of the Lord; hymn and over-exalt him into the ages'. 32.40 And the Lord-slayers too being annoyed, he says, at the little children and the crowds because, glorifying Jesus as God, they were saying: 'hosanna in the highest; blessed the one coming in the name of the Lord', he reminded them of the writing that says: 'out of the mouth of infants and sucklings you furnished praise', fitting this saying to himself and showing that glory is not unsuitably brought to him. 32.41 And angels also, he says, [...]
pass_b_english: … the ages, if not the Only-begotten? And who are those who have exchanged his glory? Those who say, “Glory to the Father through the Son in the Holy Spirit,” who glorify him as a creature and not even as eternal King.

Then he says of the same people: “So that they are without excuse; because, although they knew God, they did not glorify him as God or give thanks, but became futile in their reasonings, and their senseless heart was darkened” (Romans 1:20-21). And who is the God who was known and yet not acknowledged by heretics, Jews and Greeks, if not God the Word, who appeared in the flesh?

In his first letter to the Corinthians, too, showing that he is Lord of glory by nature, he writes thus: “For if they had known, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory” (1 Corinthians 2:8). And elsewhere: “That at the name of Jesus Christ every knee should bow, and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father” (Philippians 2:10-11), which means: he exists in the Father’s own glory.

And again: “For we see Jesus, who was made lower because of the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour” (Hebrews 2:9). This is said in inverted order. For what he means is this: Jesus, who seemed to some to have been made lower because of the suffering of death, we see crowned with glory and honour.

But he also calls him glory, since by nature he is the radiance of the Father’s glory (Hebrews 1:3), in the words he writes: “The God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory” (Ephesians 1:17). He said “God” with respect to the ineffable incarnation, and “Father” with respect to the generation that has no beginning.

And again John: “We beheld his glory, glory as of the Only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth” (John 1:14). And again in Mark, from the Saviour himself: “When the Son comes in the glory of his Father” (Mark 8:38), showing that his glory is equal in honour to the glory of the Father; and in Matthew: “When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all his angels with him” (Matthew 25:31).

And John, once more establishing that he is in glory and that glory is owed to him by all, said: “Though Jesus had done so many signs, the Jews did not believe in him, so that the word spoken through Isaiah might be fulfilled” (John 12:37-38): “Hearing you will hear, and you will by no means understand” (Isaiah 6:9). And a little further on he adds: “These things he said when he saw his glory, and he spoke of him” (John 12:41).

Peter too, in his first epistle: “Inasmuch as you share in the sufferings of Christ, rejoice, so that at the revelation of his glory you may also rejoice and exult” (1 Peter 4:13); and in the second: “Since his divine power has granted us all things that pertain to life and godliness, through the knowledge of him who called us by his own glory and virtue” (2 Peter 1:3). That is to say: the glory of the Only-begotten, the glory of his nature, of his miracles, of his kingdom and of the doxology itself, is like and equal to the glory of the Father, from whom he has been begotten by nature and without interval; and he has all things in himself as the Only-begotten, so that even when he became flesh he underwent no change or diminution.

So too the three youths, aglow not with the Babylonian flame but with longing for the Creator and Benefactor, and minding not so much the furnace that surrounded them as the Gehenna prepared for those who worship a creature, prompted creation to glorify the one who appeared with them in the furnace, of whom it is written, “And the appearance of the fourth is like the Son of God” (Daniel 3:25): “Bless the Lord, all you works of the Lord; sing his praise and exalt him above all for ever” (Daniel 3:57 LXX).

And when the Lord’s murderers, he says, were vexed with the children and the crowds because they glorified Jesus as God and said, “Hosanna in the highest; blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord” (Matthew 21:9), he reminded them of the Scripture that says, “Out of the mouth of infants and nursing babes you have prepared praise” (Psalm 8:2; Matthew 21:16). So he fitted this saying to himself and showed that glory is not offered to him unfittingly. And angels too, he says, …

choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English printed edition numbers 32.35-32.41 in the reading text, used bracket fillers ([people], [himself], [saying], [it]), abbreviated every reference, ended paragraph 32.33 with a stray 'And again...', turned ᾔδεσαν (they had known) into 'if we had known', ἅτε (since) into 'even though', made the three youths 'submit themselves to the Creation' (ὑπέβαλλον τῇ κτίσει: they prompted creation), and turned ἀχθομένων (vexed) into 'struck against the children' and μὴ ἀνοικείως (not unfittingly) into 'not inappropriately'. References: Romans 1:20 widened to 1:20-21 (the quotation runs into 1:21); 'Prayer of Azariah 1:35' made 'Daniel 3:57 LXX' (Rahlfs Greek Daniel numbering, house style); Ephesians 1:17, Hebrews 1:3, John 12:37-38 and Matthew 21:16 added; all names written in full.

choices.term: τοὺς αἰῶνας, εἰ μὴ ὁ μονογενής
choices.english: … the ages, if not the Only-begotten?
choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence (the question began in the previous section with εἰς). Only the words this section holds are translated, with a leading ellipsis.

choices.english: which means / That is to say
choices.why: Didymus' formula for introducing his own reading of a text. In 32.37 the copy-text puts his gloss in quotation marks, but it is his explanation, not Scripture, so it is not printed as a quotation.

choices.english: This is said in inverted order
choices.why: Technical term (hysteron proteron): Didymus reads 'because of the suffering of death' with 'made lower', not with 'crowned'.

choices.term: θεὸν δὲ εἶπεν τῆς ἀρρήτου σαρκώσεως, πατέρα δὲ τῆς ἀνάρχου γεννήσεως
choices.english: He said “God” with respect to the ineffable incarnation, and “Father” with respect to the generation that has no beginning
choices.why: The genitives give the ground of each title in Ephesians 1:17; 'with respect to' keeps that without adding a claim.
Keeps Didymus' play on the furnace flame: they burned with desire, not with the fire.

choices.term: οὐ μᾶλλον τὴν περιβάλλουσαν αὐτοὺς κάμινον τῆς … γεέννης προσέχοντες
choices.english: minding not so much the furnace that surrounded them as the Gehenna
choices.why: Comparative 'not more A than B': they feared Gehenna more than the furnace.
Didymus' polemical word for those who worship the Son while calling him a creature; kept as a description rather than 'idolaters', which the old draft used.
Anarthrous in Greek, but Didymus reads it of 'the one who appeared with them', the Son, so English uses 'the'.
Didymus' own harsh polemical term; kept, not softened.

choices.term: ἐδόξα σαν, ἐξο μολογήσεται, ἀρε τῇ
choices.why: Words split by line breaks in the copy-text; read as single words.
